newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba - Direct investment data should be standardised.
newsitem.headline: Buba - Direct investment data should be standardised.

text.p: Germany's Bundesbank said on Thursday that more needed to be done to introduce international standards for the calculation of direct investment flows.
The central bank said it supported current efforts being made by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to standardise statistics.
The Bundesbank added that it too would "endeavour to improve the comparability of such figures by including necessary adjustments" in its own data.

But in a section of its monthly report, the bank said that despite such efforts, there were still large discrepancies between announcement and collection methods for direct investment flows figures from country to country.

As an example, the Bundesbank said data covering 18 OECD countries for the period between 1984 and 1994 showed foreign investment from these countries in Germany at around 34.5 billion marks, while figures from the OECD countries themselves put investment in Germany at around 137 billion marks.

It said differences in data collection methods, where some systems included short-term credit contracts between countries while others didn't, and some systems included parent-unit investment flows and others did not, meant current data were not comparable.
